proposal:
# Re-rank 15 proposal (D148)

Led by the product manager seat pm-rerank-15b (Claude seat, least-recently-used rotation, D163, D164). Read only: .mob/audits/last.json (audit 108, 2026-11-01 02:02 UTC) and the four new cards.

## Before order (note 14)

228, 210, 211, 229, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 213, 217, 218, 212, 215, 206, 207

## After order

234, 228, 210, 211, 229, 230, 231, 232, 233, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 213, 217, 218, 212, 215, 206, 207

## Next card

234, the indexed process wiki, under the product owner's one-card stop-the-line waiver (D170). Fixed, not re-ranked. Card 228 (the recursive-delete scan follow-up) is next after it.

## One-line rationale

234 goes first by product owner ruling; then the cards that name an open FAIL (228, 210, 211) start; the four new cards sit behind them because none names an open FAIL, ahead of the template card 216 because each one feeds it.

## What changed against note 14

- Card 234 inserted first (D170, fixed). The waiver covers 234 only; 228, 210 and 211 resume right after it closes.
- Cards 230 to 233 inserted after 229 and before 216, in the order 230, 231, 232, 233.
- Everything else keeps note 14's order: 228, 210, 211, 229, then 216 to 207 unchanged.
- Audit 108 replaces audit 106. The open FAILs are unchanged: MD-003, MD-010, F-071, F-072, F-074. Its summary now says the re-rank 14 order is adopted and that the detect ruling, collision bug, uncommitted-work story, aider no-browser bug, pairing evaluation, wiki card and waiver are not yet recorded. That is a recording gap, not a new FAIL.

## Open FAIL check for the new cards

The corrective-card gate starts only a card that names an open FAIL (card 234 excepted, under its waiver).

| Card | Names an open FAIL? | Gate starts it? |
|---|---|---|
| 234 wiki | No (waiver D170) | Yes, by the waiver only |
| 230 one writer per checkout (bug) | No. Its source is the auditor's count of collisions, with no FAIL id | No |
| 231 uncommitted work over 30 minutes | No. It is a condition of D169 and follows card 228 (F-071), but cites no FAIL | No |
| 232 seat driver never opens a browser (bug) | No | No |
| 233 pairing tooling (spike) | No | No |

None of 230 to 233 cites MD-003, MD-010, F-071, F-072 or F-074. F-072 and F-074 are still unread by the facilitator (their ledger text is not in the repository). The audit summary's "collision bug" matches card 230's subject. If F-072 or F-074 proves to be that collision bug, 230 names it and moves up to follow 211. The same test applies to 231 and 232.

## Why this order among the new cards

- 230 first: a bug with recorded harm (3 index-lock collisions, at least 2 push races, a swept staged file, a voided vote), and it protects the push-every-commit rule and the Decider votes that every later card relies on.
- 231 second: closes the exposure D169 left open (work never committed), next to the deletion-ban work in 228.
- 232 third: a bug, but a single past occurrence (2026-10-29), with a small fix (pin the driver's flags).
- 233 last: a spike with no defect behind it; its outcome reaches the template only if kept.
- All four enable card 216, so they run before it and 216 carries them once.

## Reversals I state

- Note 14 put 216 straight after 229. I now put 230 to 233 in front of it, so the template card is not done twice. If any of the four stalls, 216 starts without it and the card enters through the normal template-change path later.
- 233 moves behind 216 if it needs more than one seat-session, because it is a spike and nothing blocks 216 on it.
- 230 moves up to follow 211 if F-072 or F-074 is confirmed as the collision bug and 230 names it. 231 and 232 move the same way if they prove to name an open FAIL.
- A FAIL that no queued card names puts its corrective first (carried from note 14).
- Carried from note 14, unchanged: 228 splits per D168 if larger than a 15 KB slice; 210 and 211 swap if no non-author reviewer can be seated for 211; 229 moves up again if a FAIL it names is confirmed.
- No card is dropped.
